MUQATIL:35:37-39/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:35:37-39/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:35:37-39/r4.claim: God made people successors after former nations; those who reject His oneness bear their own unbelief, which only increases God's anger and their loss.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p794/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p794/r5.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p794/r5.claim: The word ‘successors’ means generations that follow one another on earth.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p794/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p794/r6.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p794/r6.claim: A disbeliever bears the consequence of his disbelief and is requited with fire.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p137/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p137/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p137/r1.claim: Qatada says people are successive generations and centuries, each replacing the preceding ones on earth.

TAB-FULL:v19p388#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p388#3/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p388#3/r1.claim: God made people successors in the land after ʿĀd, Thamūd, and earlier nations, inheriting their homes and settlements.

TAB-FULL:v19p388#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p388#3/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v19p388#3/r2.claim: Qatada glosses the succession as one community after another and one generation after another.

ZAJJAJ:v4p271/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p271/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p271/r6.claim: خلفاء is the plural of خليفة: later peoples succeed earlier peoples and learn from them; a disbeliever bears the recompense of disbelief, and maqt is the strongest hatred.

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3185#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3185#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3185#2/r1.claim: Qatadah says God made people successors on earth, one community after another and one generation after another.

QUSHAYRI:v3p71/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p71/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p71/r4.claim: Each generation succeeds the one before: some are worthy bearers while others are base; the virtuous and base each test their age.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p434/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p434/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p434/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas explains that people have succeeded earlier communities as generations after those who came before.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p434/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p434/r2.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p434/r2.claim: Abu Ishaq says this community succeeds earlier ones and has seen their histories, which should serve as a lesson.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p434/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p434/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p434/r3.claim: The consequence owed for disbelief falls upon the disbeliever himself.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:35:39-42/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:35:39-42/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:35:39-42/r1.claim: God made the people successors on earth, meaning a community that came after earlier nations.

JISHUMI:v8p5854/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5854/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5854/r5.claim: Maqt is hatred; khasar is destruction or loss, also used for diminishing something.

JISHUMI:v8p5855/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5855/r11.speaker: قتادة
JISHUMI:v8p5855/r11.claim: Qatada says God made Muhammad's community successors by bringing generation after generation.

JISHUMI:v8p5855/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5855/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5855/r12.claim: Another interpretation is that this community succeeded earlier peoples, inherited what they left, and received blessings for which it should give thanks.

JISHUMI:v8p5855/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5855/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5855/r13.claim: The harm of unbelief returns to the unbeliever; further unbelief increases divine anger or punishment and increases ruin or loss.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p425#3/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p425#3/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p425#3/r2.claim: People succeed one another in the earth; alternatively, a later community witnessed former peoples and should learn from them.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p425#3/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p425#3/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p425#3/r3.claim: Disbelief brings its consequence and increases only divine wrath and loss.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p626/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p626/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p626/r1.claim: Khalifa has plural khalāʾif and khalif has plural khulafāʾ; people are God’s successors, entrusted with earthly control and its benefits so they may thank Him through unity and obedience.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p626/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p626/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p626/r2.claim: Disbelief denies this great gift and brings its consequence back on the disbeliever: God’s loathing and ultimate loss; maqt is the strongest hatred, hence the term for one marrying his father’s wife.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p626/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p626/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p626/r3.claim: The address may be to all people; alternatively, it addresses the Prophet’s audience as a nation succeeding earlier peoples and able to learn from their observed fate.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p442/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p442/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p442/r3.claim: Khalāʾif is the plural of khalīfa; fa-ʿalayhi kufruhu omits a noun, meaning the burden and harm of his disbelief fall on him.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p442/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p442/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p442/r4.claim: Maqt is contempt for someone because of a sin; arbitrary contempt without cause is not called maqt.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p442/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p442/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p442/r5.claim: Khasār is the verbal noun of losing: disbelievers lose their afterlife by ending in the Fire and punishment.

TABRISI:35:37-40/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:35:37-40/r6.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:35:37-40/r6.claim: God made the disbelievers successors, one community after another; another view says they inherited the earth after earlier generations.

TABRISI:35:37-40/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:35:37-40/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:35:37-40/r7.claim: The harm and punishment of disbelief fall on the disbeliever, and disbelief increases God’s aversion toward them and their loss and destruction.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p495#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p495#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p495#2/r1.claim: Successors in the earth are a community replacing an earlier one and able to learn from what happened to its predecessors.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p495#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p495#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p495#2/r2.claim: Whoever disbelieves bears the consequence or recompense of his disbelief.

RAZI-FULL:v26p28#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p28#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p28#2/r1.claim: Making people successors cuts off their excuse: they had time and opportunity to know, intellects, messengers who supported reason with transmitted proof, and examples in previous generations whose fate they could see.

RAZI-FULL:v26p28#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p28#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p28#2/r2.claim: Successive disbelievers incur greater abhorrence: earlier unbelievers were already hated, those warned by messengers are more culpable, and later people who witness prior punishment yet ignore it are most hated.

RAZI-FULL:v26p28#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p28#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p28#2/r3.claim: Disbelief yields only loss before God and for the unbeliever himself; a lifetime is capital, profitable when spent seeking God's pleasure and lost when spent seeking His displeasure.

QURTUBI-FULL:35:39/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:39/r1.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:35:39/r1.claim: God made people successors generation after generation and one community after another.

QURTUBI-FULL:35:39/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:39/r2.speaker: أبو بكر
QURTUBI-FULL:35:39/r2.claim: When addressed as God's caliph, Abū Bakr said he was the Messenger's successor and was content with that title.

QURTUBI-FULL:35:39/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:39/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:35:39/r3.claim: The consequence of disbelief is its punishment and torment.

QURTUBI-FULL:35:39/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:39/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:35:39/r4.claim: Maqt here means hatred and anger from God.

QURTUBI-FULL:35:39/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:39/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:35:39/r5.claim: Kufr adds only loss, ruin, and misguidance to the disbelievers.

BAYDAWI-FULL:35:38-40/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:38-40/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:38-40/r2.claim: God made humanity successive stewards entrusted with control of the earth; the term can mean one generation after another or caliphs.

BAYDAWI-FULL:35:38-40/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:38-40/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:38-40/r3.claim: Disbelief's two consequences are independent: God's intense aversion and loss in the afterlife, so repetition emphasizes that each alone requires avoidance.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p345#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p345#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p345#4/r1.claim: God made people successors on earth, giving them authority over its resources and benefits so they would thank Him through monotheism and obedience.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p345#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p345#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p345#4/r2.claim: Disbelief's consequence returns to the unbeliever as divine anger and loss in the next life; anger means intense hatred, and loss means ruin.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p36#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p36#2/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p36#2/r11.claim: «Successors» can be plural of khalīfa or khalīf; humanity replaces earlier peoples, yet fails to learn from destroyed deniers of the messengers.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p36#2/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p36#2/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p36#2/r12.claim: A disbeliever bears the punishment of his disbelief; the address is apparently general, though some restrict it to Meccans.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p36#2/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p36#2/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p36#2/r13.claim: «Maqt» means the strongest contempt, hatred, and anger; loss is loss of a lifetime spent outside obedience, exchanged for God’s wrath and Hell instead of reward.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p557/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p557/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p557/r2.claim: God makes generations succeed earlier peoples, as also stated in 27:62.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p557/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p557/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p557/r3.claim: The harm of disbelief returns to the disbeliever; continued disbelief increases God's anger and the unbelievers' loss, whereas believers who live and act well rise in rank, reward, and God's love.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p231/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p231/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p231/r1.claim: A khalīfa succeeds another person in the work that person had been doing; this explains humanity as generations succeeding one another.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p231/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p231/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p231/r10.claim: The disbelievers use the term nikāḥ al-maqt for marrying their fathers' wives, yet show no concern about earning God's contempt despite His beneficence.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p231/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p231/r2.speaker: الأصبهاني
BIQAI-FULL:v6p231/r2.claim: He explains that khulafāʾ is the plural of khalīf.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p231/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p231/r3.speaker: القشيري
BIQAI-FULL:v6p231/r3.claim: Each age succeeds the previous one; some generations honor their predecessors, while others are base and disgraceful, and the virtuous and vile each test their age.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p231/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p231/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p231/r4.claim: God's repeated deaths and succession keep even many generations from filling the earth; without death, reproduction over time would outgrow it, though humans began as a small part of its soil.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p231/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p231/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p231/r5.claim: God alone lets people inhabit and manage their portion of the earth, so they owe Him gratitude rather than disbelief.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p231/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p231/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p231/r6.claim: Disbelief harms only the disbeliever, who repudiates a precious blessing despite knowing that God alone enabled it.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p231/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p231/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p231/r7.claim: Here kāfirūn means those who cover the truth; their disbelief is entrenched, unlike a temporary disbelief that might end in faith.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p231/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p231/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p231/r8.claim: Their disbelief increases only maqt: God deals with them as one who hates and despises intensely, the consequence signified by the divine attribute.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p231/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p231/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p231/r9.claim: The divine descriptions convey their ultimate consequences and are framed in their harshest sense to repel people from the causes of such consequences.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p232/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p232/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p232/r1.claim: Disbelief brings loss in this world and the next, in wealth and self, the ultimate result of divine contempt.

DURR-FULL:v7p31/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p31/r6.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p31/r6.claim: Qatada says God made people successors, one community and generation after another.

BURSEVI:v7p280/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p280/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p280/r1.claim: God made people successors in His earth, empowered to manage it and use its benefits, or heirs to earlier nations’ worldly goods so they may give thanks through monotheism and obedience.

BURSEVI:v7p280/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p280/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p280/r2.claim: Ishari reading: every person, excellent or base, is God’s vicegerent; the excellent reflect divine artistry in godly character and inspired knowledge, the base in crafts and handiwork.

BURSEVI:v7p280/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p280/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p280/r3.claim: Human vicegerency includes transforming created materials: God creates wheat and cotton, while people grind and bake the wheat or spin and weave the cotton.

BURSEVI:v7p280/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p280/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p280/r4.claim: Disbelief betrays the trust of vicegerency by opposing its Lord and following desire; its punishment, including expulsion, curse, and Fire, falls only on the disbeliever.

BURSEVI:v7p280/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p280/r5.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v7p280/r5.claim: Al-Raghib defines مقت as intense hatred for someone seen committing an ugly act.

BURSEVI:v7p280/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p280/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p280/r6.claim: Disbelief independently increases both divine loathing and loss, the latter being deprivation of Paradise; repetition emphasizes each consequence and the indefinite nouns magnify them.

ALUSI-FULL:v22p202/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p202/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p202/r1.claim: God made people successors entrusted with disposal and enjoyment of the earth's resources.

ALUSI-FULL:v22p202/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p202/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p202/r10.claim: The increase of loss is in the hereafter.

ALUSI-FULL:v22p202/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p202/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p202/r11.claim: The two repeated clauses explain the consequence of disbelief; repetition reinforces the warning because divine abhorrence and loss each independently establish its ugliness.

ALUSI-FULL:v22p202/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p202/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p202/r2.claim: The verse can mean that later peoples succeeded earlier nations and inherited their worldly goods so they would give thanks through monotheism and obedience.

ALUSI-FULL:v22p202/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p202/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p202/r3.claim: It can also mean replacing nations who denied messengers and were destroyed, so people should learn from their fate.

ALUSI-FULL:v22p202/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p202/r4.speaker: البحر
ALUSI-FULL:v22p202/r4.claim: Al-Baḥr takes the address as general; another view restricts it to the people of Mecca.

ALUSI-FULL:v22p202/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p202/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p202/r5.claim: Khalāʾif is the regular broken plural of khalīfa; khulafāʾ is usually the plural of khalīf, though al-Wāḥidī also allows it for khalīfa.

ALUSI-FULL:v22p202/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p202/r6.speaker: الواحدي
ALUSI-FULL:v22p202/r6.claim: Al-Wāḥidī permits khulafāʾ as a plural of khalīfa, contrary to the better-known analysis.

ALUSI-FULL:v22p202/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p202/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p202/r7.claim: Disbelief means either scorning this great blessing or persisting in unbelief and abandoning faith after being guided.

ALUSI-FULL:v22p202/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p202/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p202/r8.claim: The consequence of disbelief falls on the disbeliever alone, not anyone else.

ALUSI-FULL:v22p202/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p202/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p202/r9.claim: Maqt means the severest contempt, hatred, and anger.

ELMALILI:35:38-45#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:35:38-45#2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:35:38-45#2/r1.claim: God made the community successors on earth and entrusted them with carrying out divine law.

ELMALILI:35:38-45#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:35:38-45#2/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:35:38-45#2/r2.claim: The verse is a miraculous unseen promise that the community of Muhammad would govern in the future, a great blessing.

ELMALILI:35:38-45#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:35:38-45#2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:35:38-45#2/r3.claim: Disbelief in response to this blessing harms only the disbeliever, who bears its penalty.

ELMALILI:35:38-45#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:35:38-45#2/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:35:38-45#2/r4.claim: Disbelief increases divine abhorrence and loss because faithlessness is both deprivation and a cause of ruin.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p320/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p320/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p320/r6.claim: The statement that God knows the unseen links His knowledge of believers and servants to the next argument about the alleged partners, while recapping the earlier proof of His care and knowledge.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p321/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p321/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p321/r5.claim: ‘He is the One who made you successors on earth’ is parenthetical between the statement of God's knowledge and the consequence for disbelief.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p321/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p321/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p321/r6.claim: Khalāʾif means successors: one possibility is that later human generations followed earlier peoples, including all groups, which also shows that God knows those He created.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p321/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p321/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p321/r7.claim: Alternatively, khalāʾif means people given authority over the earth; Ibn ʿĀshūr reads this as good news of Muslim political rule and Islam's eventual ascendancy.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p322/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p322/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p322/r1.claim: The nominal sentence strengthens the assertion that God made the addressees successors on earth.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p322/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p322/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p322/r2.claim: The conditional ‘whoever disbelieves, his disbelief is against him’ indirectly signals that God does not depend on their ceasing to disbelieve.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p322/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p322/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p322/r3.claim: The clause about increased contempt explains the preceding clause but is coordinated as an independent assertion to emphasize it.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p322/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p322/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p322/r4.claim: Maqt is hatred mixed with humiliation; God's ‘hatred’ figuratively means withdrawing His grace and imposing severe punishment.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p322/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p322/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p322/r5.claim: The apparent paradox is resolved by taking repeated disbelief as persistence over time: the polytheists boasted they would not follow Muslims, and God answers that their continued disbelief increases contempt and loss.

TABATABAI:35:39-41/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:35:39-41/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:35:39-41/r1.claim: The closing section argues for God's sole lordship from human succession on earth and His sustaining the heavens and earth, denies lordship to idols, rebukes broken oaths and plotting, and warns that God delays but does not fail to punish.

TABATABAI:35:39-41/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:35:39-41/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:35:39-41/r2.claim: Each human generation succeeds its predecessor and gains comparable use of the earth; this succession is bound to procreation and creation, so it is a form of governance inseparable from creation.

TABATABAI:35:39-41/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:35:39-41/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:35:39-41/r3.claim: Because God creates humanity and makes generations successors, He alone governs them; even opponents concede that God is the Creator, so He is their Lord.

TABATABAI:35:39-41/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:35:39-41/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:35:39-41/r4.claim: Disbelief harms the disbeliever by bringing divine contempt and personal loss, replacing human happiness with misery in the journey to the next life.

TABATABAI:35:39-41/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:35:39-41/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:35:39-41/r5.claim: The text says contempt is 'with their Lord' because it comes from God, while loss is the person's own consequence of changing faith and happiness into disbelief and misery.

TABATABAI:35:39-41/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:35:39-41/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:35:39-41/r6.claim: The wording 'increase' reflects human nature as open to development: faith increases perfection and nearness to God, while disbelief increases contempt and loss.

TABATABAI:35:39-41/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:35:39-41/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:35:39-41/r7.claim: Divine love and hatred are attributes of action, not intrinsic qualities: love is mercy extending toward someone and hatred is its withdrawal.

ASAD-NOTES:35:38#n24/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:35:38#n24/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:35:38#n24/r1.claim: Inheriting the earth means humanity has been given the ability to distinguish right from wrong and truth from falsehood.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p263/r10.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p263/r10.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p263/r10.claim: The affluent reject the Qur'an because they mistake worldly wealth and status for proof of divine favor and assume it guarantees success in the next life.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p263/r11.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p263/r11.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p263/r11.claim: Worldly favors test whether people are grateful; in the Hereafter each person is judged by deeds.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p264/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p264/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p264/r1.claim: In the Hereafter God deals with each person according to their deeds.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p297/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p297/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p297/r3.claim: The following passage answers opponents' objections and demands, then points to the inevitable fate of those denying truth through doubts.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p307/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p307/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p307/r1.claim: The repeated opening about provision has different force: verse 36 stresses God's control and the test of gratitude or patience, so people should neither boast nor despair.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p307/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p307/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p307/r2.claim: Verse 39 tells the affluent to spend God's blessings on what pleases Him; no amount spent in His way is wasted, and He repays it.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p307/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p307/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p307/r3.claim: The phrase “in God's way” is omitted after “whatever you spend” because context supplies it; “God replaces for you” means He returns what was lost.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p307/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p307/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p307/r4.claim: God is the best provider assures spenders that their small gifts will receive a recompense they cannot yet imagine; “best” states an attribute rather than comparison.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p363/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p363/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p363/r1.claim: The Quraysh’s political leadership in Arabia is neither their own achievement nor unprecedented; earlier arrogant disbelieving nations were destroyed, and they have succeeded those nations.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p363/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p363/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p363/r2.claim: God’s standard for the rise and fall of nations is impartial; the Quraysh will repeat the history of the nations whose accounts they heard.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p363/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p363/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p363/r3.claim: If the Quraysh imitate earlier nations’ arrogance and disbelief, they should expect the same fate.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:38/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:38/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:38/r1.claim: After affirming God’s limitless knowledge and humanity’s earthly role, the passage challenges idolaters to prove their gods created anything, share in the heavens, or have divine authorization; claims that idols, angels, or humans will intercede are delusions. The term khalifa is linked to 2:30.

STUDYQURAN:35:39/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:35:39/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:35:39/r1.claim: As God made Adam a vicegerent, He appoints all humanity as vicegerents upon earth.

STUDYQURAN:35:39/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:35:39/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:35:39/r2.claim: Humanity’s vicegerency connects to the reminder that God made the earth’s contents subservient to people.

STUDYQURAN:35:39/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:35:39/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:35:39/r3.claim: Disbelief harms only its holder and relates to the principle that no one bears another’s burden, because no one carries another’s disbelief.

STUDYQURAN:35:39/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:35:39/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:35:39/r4.claim: Disbelief also rejects humanity’s true nature and responsibility toward God, given its vicegerent role.

STUDYQURAN:35:39/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:35:39/r5.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:35:39/r5.claim: The longer disbelievers persist, the more they will lose on the Day of Resurrection; this explains their growing odium.

STUDYQURAN:35:39/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:35:39/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:35:39/r6.claim: Other passages show messengers’ calls increasing disbelievers’ opposition and other negative reactions.

STUDYQURAN:35:intro/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:35:intro/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:35:intro/r9.claim: The longest comparison of believers and disbelievers in verses 29–39 leads into a final contrast between God’s Power and idols, then the outcomes of disbelief.
